## Result

- Skill: design-review.
- Review status: approved.
- Package members: Release model at docs/design/release/release.md and directly affected operational guidance docs/releases/README.md. Other subjects are explicit supporting direction/evidence and unchanged plan context.
- Upstream review ID: direct user-authorized correction to adopted Release direction, as in r1; no new Proposal Review selected.
- Review ID and round: design-review-r2, round2.
- Material findings: none at Design scope.
- Correction targets: none for this package.
- Recording status: recorded upon successful targeted save.
- Open blockers: none to Design approval; implementation concerns and actual PR/main proof remain pending.
- Immediate next stage: route-owned current Delivery reliance and implementation assessment.
- Claim limitations: exact Design package only; no corrected implementation, CI pass, Verify, PR or publication authority.

## Actual independence and basis

This reviewer authored no model, guidance, plan or implementation. Its prior contribution was independent Delivery/Code Review diagnosis; the Design clarification was authored by a different agent. Identifying a requirement gap did not author its chosen disposition. Read the complete Release model and release-operation guidance, exact clarification, prior independent Design r1, current unchanged primary plan and relevant recorded preparation failure basis. Read packaged assessment, reliance, Test and recording guidance. No engineering/routing edits are made. Preserve r1 original judgment and subjects; mark its applicability stale because the normative offline/public distinction changed.

## Whole-package coherence

The revised ordinary-CI section now owns a precise applicability distinction. Offline CI validates stable source identity, intent syntax/required rationale, supported decision vocabulary and source-package agreement. It expressly does not establish increment eligibility against latest public state. Hosted Release still obtains that actual state and enforces the existing decision/increment rules before preparing the exact merged publication candidate. Thus an offline pass on a declared decision is not a claim that the declaration matches a currently observed public predecessor. Missing/contradictory authored package facts and unknown values remain rejection cases.

This is an explicit owner-selected refinement of r1's ambiguous instruction to apply all existing version-decision rules offline. It is not a retroactive assertion that the earlier implementation complied with r1, nor a waiver of REL-SR02 at publication. Ordinary CI must remain usable when the same source version is already public; inventing a public baseline from a fixture or requiring registry access for offline checks would misstate that authority. Candidate preparation still has no publication-state query under REL-SR05; hosted input resolution owns the public observation outside that helper.

CI candidates must carry CI-only identity and be rejected by publication approval validation. They cannot be promoted or stripped of their limitation to reuse premerge authority. Hosted preparation regenerates from the exact merged source with public eligibility checked, then one protected candidate-specific approval remains required. The representative scenarios explicitly require CI-only publication rejection and hosted invalid-increment rejection. These are credible executable safeguards, not just prose claim limits. All actual selected PR and direct-main checks, negative/integrity coverage, source immutability, exact packed runtime and prepared-subject reporting remain mandatory.

The current README states only that ordinary CI checks an isolated package and hosted preparation produces the later approved candidate; it does not promise offline registry eligibility or promote PR artifacts. Its zero GitHub approving-review policy preserves independent engineering assessment and Verify, with protected release approval separate. No further README amendment or new model owner is necessary. Existing source-displacement maps, decisions, historical representations, identity chain, timing policy, evidence-ref recovery and one-approval publication remain unchanged. No historic source restoration, additional retirement, remote configuration or new runner follows.

## Delivery applicability and proof consequence

The primary plan is unchanged at ce52cafa7d128c46dae9f28bc19dd4cfb91280df28d8f02e03113cc568c61629. Its M1 invalid-intent/subject regressions, preserved actual PR/main checks, no publication authority and existing release-suite proof can implement the clarified boundary without new work or reordered milestones. The prior Delivery review relied on the older Design identity, so its current reliance must be renewed; no plan rewrite is required merely to restate the owning rule. The renewal must explicitly map CI-only rejection and retained hosted increment-mismatch regression into M1 before approval of implementation. This Design approval alone does not supply that Delivery decision.

The previously reported runtime/test-mutation acceptance and range-normalization defects remain Code Review concerns. Author reports of corrections and focused tests are not independently approved here. Actual same-subject PR/main runs, integrity negatives and final whole-change Code Review/Verify remain required. Current helper changes are only feasibility context and are not included as approved engineering members.

## Checks and handoff

Actually performed complete member reads, exact delta/package comparison, scoped CLI context/subject inspect and targeted recording. No runtime command or external registry query was executed for this Design assessment; no passing implementation/CI result is inferred. Scoped record validation and git diff --check follow save. Return to route and responsible Delivery/implementation reviewers. R1 remains original/stale, and no old judgment is retargeted.
independence_basis: Independent nonauthor assessed clarification authored by a different agent; prior participation was review diagnosis only, with no model/guidance/plan/code authorship.
